title: The Far Passage
premise: Mara Okafor, who left her archaeologist father's shadow twenty years ago to become the best high-altitude guide nobody's heard of, is handed a dying prospector's map and a promise she can't refuse: carry it across the Karakor-like Serrano Range before the snows seal the passes. The map points to a buried expedition cache that includes her father's lost final journals — proof he wasn't the fraud history remembers. Racing a rival salvage crew and the early monsoon, Mara discovers the 'treasure' is testimony: her father recorded how his partner survived by abandoning eleven men, and the partner's grandson is the rival on her trail. At the pass, with the storm breaking, Mara must choose between destroying the truth to protect a family or publishing it at the cost of everything she's built; she chooses the truth, buries her father beside the mountain instead of the myth, and walks down into the monsoon finally measuring life in years.
about_author: Oscar Voss is the pen name of a former logistics coordinator for Himalayan survey expeditions who spent a decade moving supplies over passes most people only photograph from below. He writes adventure fiction in a converted shipping container in Kathmandu, where the monsoon gives him four months a year to type.

chapters.title: The Weight of Miles
chapters.summary: Mara guides a paying client over a 5,000-meter pass, calculating distances instead of feeling them. A radio call summons her to Leh, where an old debt waits. POV: Mara. Beat: competence as armor, restlessness beneath.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Ledger
chapters.summary: In a Leh hospice, prospector Tomas Reyes shows her a hand-drawn map and names her father, Elias Okafor, dead twenty years and disgraced. He trades the map for a promise: deliver what's in the cache to whoever deserves it. POV: Mara. Beat: the past knocking with cold hands.

chapters.title: What the Map Costs
chapters.summary: Reyes dies before dawn. Mara studies the map: a route through the Serrano Range to a cache marked with her father's initials. She recognizes the rival crew's supply purchases in town — someone else has the same destination. POV: Mara. Beat: grief disguised as logistics.

chapters.title: The Grandson
chapters.summary: She meets Devan Reyes at the outfitter's, polite and armed with his grandfather's half of the story: Elias Okafor abandoned eleven men on the mountain. They agree, warily, to share the route but not the prize. POV: Mara. Beat: distrust wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Packing for Ghosts
chapters.summary: Mara provisions obsessively, then finds her father's old compass in her storage locker — a thing she swore she'd sold. She packs it anyway. Her best porter, Tsering, signs on despite the late season. POV: Mara. Beat: inheritance arriving against her will.

chapters.title: Into the Foothills
chapters.summary: The team of five enters the range through terraced valleys. Devan's crew shadows them a day behind. First night, Mara dreams of her father's hands brushing dirt from pottery. POV: Mara. Beat: the familiar country of leaving.

chapters.title: Tsering's Question
chapters.summary: Tsering asks why she really came. Mara lies about the fee; he lets the lie stand, which is worse than calling it. They cross the first river in spate, losing a food barrel. POV: Mara. Beat: intimacy as exposure.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: In a high village, an old woman recognizes the name Okafor and spits. Her grandfather was one of the eleven. Mara learns the abandonment happened not far ahead. POV: Mara. Beat: shame inherited like altitude sickness.

chapters.title: Devan's Version
chapters.summary: Devan catches up at a shepherd camp; over tea they trade stories. His grandfather survived the descent and never spoke of it. Both realize neither knows what actually happened above the icefall. POV: alternating Mara/Devan. Beat: two heirs, one wound.

chapters.title: The Icefall
chapters.summary: A serac collapse nearly kills Tsering; Mara's route-finding saves him. The team's trust in her deepens even as she hides the map's second annotation — a date, three days after the abandonment. POV: Mara. Beat: guilt sharpened by rescue.

chapters.title: Camp Above Clouds
chapters.summary: Rest day. Mara reads the compass inscription: To E.O., who digs where others won't. She admits to herself she wants vindication more than treasure. Snow begins falling out of season. POV: Mara. Beat: wanting, confessed only inwardly.

chapters.title: The Second Annotation
chapters.summary: Tsering sees the map's hidden date and confronts her: what is she not telling them? Mara deflects; the team's cohesion cracks. Devan's crew passes their camp without stopping, heads down, empty-handed. POV: Mara. Beat: secrets costing altitude.

chapters.title: Why They Turned Back
chapters.summary: A note left in Devan's abandoned cook tent reveals his crew mutinied — the monsoon is coming weeks early and they think he's chasing a ghost. Devan asks to join Mara's rope team. She says no. POV: Devan. Beat: pride choosing solitude.

chapters.title: The Moraine Field
chapters.summary: They reach the moraine where the eleven were last seen alive. Mara finds a rusted stove plate stamped with the expedition mark. Tsering quietly begins helping her search, unasked. POV: Mara. Beat: archaeology as mourning.

chapters.title: First Bones
chapters.summary: Wind scours a slope, exposing remains and a rotted rucksack containing a water flask engraved with a woman's initials — one of the eleven was Elias's wife, Mara's mother, whom Mara believed died years later, elsewhere. POV: Mara. Beat: the ground rewriting her childhood.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Radio confirms the monsoon's northern surge; they have perhaps six days before the passes close. Tsering votes to turn back. Mara refuses. The team splits the vote and follows her anyway, unhappily. POV: Tsering. Beat: leadership as coercion.

chapters.title: The Couloir
chapters.summary: A rockfall injures porter Dorje's arm. Mara sets it under firelight while he curses her ambition. She tells him, finally, about her father. It doesn't fix anything, but they sleep. POV: Dorje. Beat: confession without absolution.

chapters.title: The Cache Door
chapters.summary: Above the icefall they find it: a cairn-sealed crevice, her father's initials chiseled beside it. Inside, sealed tins — journals, photographs, and a ledger of supplies meant to sustain survivors who never arrived. POV: Mara. Beat: the door to everything.

chapters.title: Elias's Hand
chapters.summary: By headlamp, Mara reads the first journal pages: her father's voice, precise and warm, describing the route and his excitement about the dig. She laughs and cries at once. Then the entries darken. POV: Mara. Beat: reunion with a voice.

chapters.title: What Happened Above the Icefall
chapters.summary: The journals reveal it: Reyes senior panicked in a whiteout and cut the rope line, stranding the eleven — including Mara's mother, who'd insisted on coming. Elias stayed with the stranded, digging them a shelter; he froze rather than descend alone. POV: Mara. Beat: the inversion of everything.

chapters.title: The Lie That Survived
chapters.summary: Reyes senior made it down and told the world Elias abandoned the men. The journals are the only proof. Devan arrives alone at the cache, having followed their track, and reads over her shoulder. POV: Devan. Beat: inheritance detonating twice.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Mountain
chapters.summary: Devan refuses to believe it; his grandfather was his hero. He demands the journals. Mara refuses. They face each other over the open tin as snow thickens. Tsering intervenes: neither leaves until the storm breaks. POV: Devan. Beat: grief turning to siege.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Three days pinned in the cache shelter, air thin, fuel low. Devan and Mara take watch shifts together and talk — childhoods shaped by other people's mountains. Something like respect forms. POV: alternating. Beat: enemies sharing a fire.

chapters.title: Dorje's Fever
chapters.summary: Dorje's injured arm infects. They must move or lose him. The storm lifts briefly; Mara calculates a descent window of hours. Devan offers his rope and knowledge of the lower route. She accepts. POV: Tsering. Beat: survival forcing alliance.

chapters.title: The Descent Begins
chapters.summary: They lower Dorje down the couloir in worsening light. Mara carries the journals against her spine. A slip nearly takes Devan; Mara holds the rope and doesn't let go. POV: Mara. Beat: the promise kept in muscle, not words.

chapters.title: The Glacier Crossing
chapters.summary: A hidden crevasse field, softened by melt. Tsering probes; they inch across. Mara reads aloud from the journal to keep morale up — her mother's voice appears in the margins, annotating her husband's notes. POV: Mara. Beat: the dead encouraging the living.

chapters.title: Monsoon Landfall
chapters.summary: The wall of rain hits the foothills below them; rivers rise behind. They descend into the storm's edge, soaked, hypothermic, moving. Devan stops arguing about the journals. Getting down becomes the whole world. POV: Devan. Beat: nature erasing stakes except one.

chapters.title: The River
chapters.summary: The crossing they used on the way in is now impassable. They build a rope traverse in driving rain; Dorje goes first, weakest. Halfway, the anchor shifts. Tsering swims the flood to re-set it. POV: Tsering. Beat: courage as ordinary labor.

chapters.title: What Deserves Delivering
chapters.summary: Sheltering in a cave, Mara realizes Reyes's promise said deliver to whoever deserves it — and both heirs now know the truth belongs to the families of the eleven, not to either of them. Devan agrees. POV: Mara. Beat: ownership dissolving into duty.

chapters.title: The Village Again
chapters.summary: They return to the high village. Mara kneels before the old woman and gives her the ledger of the eleven — names, ration weights, last entries. The woman reads her grandfather's handwriting and weeps. POV: Mara. Beat: restitution, insufficient and real.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: In the valley town, a publisher's agent hears rumors and offers money for exclusive rights to the story. Accepting means controlling the narrative — and repeating the old crime of deciding whose memory counts. POV: Mara. Beat: temptation in a clean shirt.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Mara and Devan publish the journals jointly and freely, sending copies to every descendant of the eleven and to the mountaineering archives. The expeditions' histories begin to be rewritten. Neither profits. POV: Devan. Beat: truth given away as wealth.

chapters.title: Burying Elias
chapters.summary: Mara returns to the moraine with Tsering and intercedes with monks to perform rites at the site. She leaves the compass there, needle finally pointing home. She speaks to her father's bones for the first time. POV: Mara. Beat: burial as arrival.

chapters.title: Devan's Goodbye
chapters.summary: At the trailhead, Devan tells her he's taking his grandfather's remaining maps to find the other places Elias dug — restoring the record piece by piece. They part as something rarer than friends: co-authors of a correction. POV: Devan. Beat: enmity composted into purpose.

chapters.title: Tsering's Terms
chapters.summary: Tsering agrees to work with her again on one condition: no more secrets carried above base camp. Mara hires him at full partnership. The team disperses; Dorje salutes her with his splinted arm. POV: Tsering. Beat: trust rebuilt on new terms.

chapters.title: The Long Letter
chapters.summary: Mara writes to the descendants of all eleven, answering letters for months. One reply comes from a man who thought his grandmother had run off — she hadn't; she'd been on the mountain. Grief and gratitude arrive together. POV: Mara. Beat: memory distributed among the living.

chapters.title: Measuring Years
chapters.summary: Spring again. Mara plants a garden at her Leh house for the first time in twenty years of transit — a thing measured in seasons, not miles. She still guides, but she comes back now. POV: Mara. Beat: the quiet after the climb.

chapters.title: The Far Passage
chapters.summary: A young climber arrives asking about the Okafor route, famous now. Mara leads her up it, pointing out the cairn, telling the true story plainly. On the summit she measures nothing at all. POV: Mara. Beat: legacy handed forward, weight set down.

chapters.title: Coda: What the Mountain Keeps
chapters.summary: Years later, Tsering's daughter finds Mara's published edition of the journals in a school library, her mother's marginalia printed alongside Elias's hand. The mountain keeps its dead; the living keep each other. POV: omniscient. Beat: inheritance completed — memory, honestly priced.
